A small piece of heaven for a family broken by tragedy. In July, Sierra Sharry and Lane Smith were about to welcome their baby. Sharry was eight months pregnant. Then, Smith fell and hit his head. He was taken to OU Medical Center in Oklahoma City, but didn’t survive. "July 13th, 2014, was the worst day of my life," Sharry wrote on Facebook. "I lost my best friend. The father of my unborn child." Their son, Taos, was born a few weeks later. When it was time for his 6-month photo, Sharry asked the photographer to help make their family feel complete, just for one picture.

You probably already have an opinion about Indiana's religious freedom law. You may agree with many companies that are criticizing the law, saying it lets businesses turn away gay and lesbian people under the excuse of religion.. Or, like Indiana Governor Mike Pence, you might be surprised by the anger and say the law is just like one already used at the federal level and in 19 other states. The law is controversial because the discussion about religious freedom and gay rights is always emotional. Also, people are questioning what the law really means and why it was created.

Some fans of Lucille Ball want her statue removed from a park in her hometown, because they think it looks unpretty and doesn’t match her famous image. The life-size bronze statue in Celoron, New York, has been criticized and compared to singer Conway Twitty, the snake from "Beetlejuice," and actor Steve Buscemi—others have said it looks like a few other odd things. Even the mayor, Scott Schrecengost, has said he doesn’t like it. The statue shows Lucille Ball holding a bottle of a fake drink called Vitameatavegamin, from her "I Love Lucy" show. The last time Muhammadu Buhari became president in Nigeria, he took power by force. This time, he won through a fair election. Here are five reasons why this election, one of the most heated in Nigeria’s history, matters so much. For the first time ever, the opposition party defeated the ruling party in a democratic election. Muhammadu Buhari, who is 77, won the presidential election, beating the outgoing president, Goodluck Jonathan, by about two million votes. Nigeria is important because it has the largest economy and most people in Africa. It is also one of Africa’s biggest oil producers and sends a lot of crude oil to the United States.

People in Iran were extremely excited, almost like they had won a major world event. But what happened was even more important. Iranians celebrated after a major nuclear deal was reached with the United States and other countries. This deal could end years of tough international sanctions and stop Iran’s isolation. The celebrations started late on Thursday. In Tehran, on Vali Asr Street, one of the city’s main roads, people waved flags from car roofs, played loud music, and used the hashtag #IranTalks online. Car horns honked, men danced in the middle of traffic, and some people showed off U States dollar bills.

A fourth man, Dilkhayot Kasimov, has been charged in connection with a plot to help terrorists and to join ISIS, according to a new indictment from a federal court in Brooklyn. The indictment adds Kasimov to a previous case against three other men: Abdurasul Hasanovich Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov. These three men were charged with two counts of supporting a foreign terrorist group. They have all pleaded not guilty. It is not known whether Kasimov has been arrested.

CNN reported that the third blood moon in a four-part series was the shortest eclipse.. The moon fully entered Earth's shadow at 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. ET) on Saturday, causing a total lunar eclipse that lasted just under five minutes—the shortest total lunar eclipse of the century, according to NASA. Before, during, and after the eclipse, the moon had a burnt-orange color, which is why total eclipses are called "blood moons."

Istanbul, Turkey (CNN)  
On Tuesday, many Turks were scared and confused. An older woman wearing a white headscar and carrying shopping bags stood outside a busy subway station in Istanbul. she asked, "What's happening? Why can't I get in?" She was one of millions affected by the worst power outage in Turkey in over ten years.  
Dozens of cities lost electricity for many hours. Millions of people were affected, including train and subway passengers who were stuck because the systems stopped working.

During this Holy Week, let’s remember what the Bible says about fair pay. The book of Isaiah says that true fasting means breaking unfair chains, ending workplace abuse, freeing those who are oppressed, and canceling debts. McDonald's decision to raise wages for 90,000 workers is a big step forward for fast-food cooks and cashiers, and for everyone who supports them. When workers stand together, they make it harder for successful companies like McDonald's to pay wages so low that workers can't escape poverty.

California may soon be known for the color of its lawns— brown. Governor Jerry Brown has imposed mandatory water cuts for the first time. This affects residents, businesses, and farms. Cities and towns across the state must cut their water use by 25%..... "The idea of your nice green grass getting water every day is over," Brown said. The 25% reduction means about 1.5 million acre-feet of water will be saved over the next nine months. (.. An acre-foot of water is about 325,000 gallons.

London (CNN) – Voters in the UK have little time left to choose their next government. as polling stations open across the country in a fast-moving election that could shift the political scene. The campaign has been very short, especially compared to the long U.S. election cycles. The result could be a change from David Cameron’s Conservative Party to the Labour Party, led by Ed Miliband – or a complex process as leaders try to form deals with smaller parties. But we won’t know the outcome until after the polls close late Thursday evening, local time.

This time of year, Christians around the world—over 2 billion of us—think about the death and resurrection of Jesus. This Holy Week, because of the deadly attack on Christian students in Kenya and recent threats against Christians in other countries, we are asking Christians to also remember how many Christians and others have suffered because of their faith. These include people who have been cruced, beheaded, stoned, forced into slavery, sexually abused, trafficked, harassed, bombed, or driven from their homes. All because they are Christians.

Three Ferguson, Missouri, city employees — including a top court clerk and two police officers — were either fired or resigned after racist and offensive emails they sent were made public. The emails were found during a U.S. Justice Department investigation into racism in Ferguson’s police and court systems. The messages contained racist remarks about President Barack Obama, First Lady Michelle Obama, Muslims, and other minorities. The emails were obtained by the Washington Post through a public records request on Thursday and were reviewed by CNN on Friday. The officers involved were Police Captain Rick Henke and Sergeant [name not provided].

Two people, including a licensed greyhound trainer, have been arrested in Australia after at least 55 dog bodies were found dumped in the bush in Queensland. The two suspects are from Bundaberg – 77-year-old man and a 64-year-old woman. Each was charged with one count of illegal possession of a firearm, according to ABC. The woman, who is a licensed greyhound trainer, was also charged with trying to stop police. Michael Beatty, from RSPCA Queensland, said the investigation is still ongoing. RSPCA is helping Queensland police with the case.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their Wisconsin town. They sell frozen pizzas, including breakfast and gluten-free ones, and got them into stores in Nichols, which is west of Green Bay. They built a loyal customer base. But this week, their business was at risk because some people confused them with Memories Pizza in Walkerton, Indiana. That restaurant made national news when its owners said they would not cater a same-sex wedding. People posted angry messages on Memories Gourmet Pizza's Facebook page and called the business to protest.

Archaeologists in Austria found the complete skeleton of a camel, believed to have been used by Ottoman soldiers during the 17th century siege of Vienna.. The remains were discovered in 2006-2007 under a cellar while digging at the construction site for a shopping center in the city of Tulln.... The team was from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna (Vetmeduni).. The skeleton was partially uncovered. At first, experts thought it might be a large horse or cow. But after looking at the neck bones, lower jaw, and forearm bones, archaeozoologist Alfred Galik said it was clearly a camel.

Andrew Getty, the 4-year-old grandson of J. Paul Getty, died Tuesday afternoon at his home in Los Angeles. His parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, said in a statement that they asked the media and the public to respect their privacy during this hard time. The Los Angeles County coroner's office, through assistant chief Ed Winter, said Getty's death "appears to be from natural causes or an accident." Some medicine was found at Getty's home, but officials don't know if he was taking it or what his health history was.

We may never fully understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9424 into the French Alps on March 24, killing everyone on board. The most recent report shows he made the plane descend quickly toward the ground. It’s very frightening. As the investigation continues, we will learn more about how much he hid his mental illness, or how much help he asked for. We’ll also find out how much his depression affected his ability to fly. Should he have quit his job? Should his doctors have warned someone? His case brings up big and important questions about people with mental illness and the shame and fear that often come with it.

(CNN) He didn't give his real name. But the name tattooed on his neck — Gertrude — gave him away. That's what Kankakee County, Illinois, Sheriff Tim Bukowski said Saturday about Kamron Taylor, the 23-year-old who was convicted of murder and had escaped from jail. He was caught overnight in Chicago. Authorities across Illinois had been searching for Taylor since early Wednesday, when he attacked a correctional officer at the Kankakee County's Jerome Combs Detention Center,, then ran away with the officer's uniform and SUV. The last time officials saw Taylor was on surveillance video. Just before midnight Friday, he was spotted in Chicago. "They saw a man who matched the description," Bukowski said.

As his military career comes to an end, Britain's Prince Harry is heading to Australia. The 30-year-old prince will arrive on Monday for a four-week stay with the Australian armed forces. He will work and live with Australian Army soldiers in regiments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth, according to the Australian Defence Forces. Harry has previously spent time with Australian troops on several occasions during his 10-year military service, a spokesman said.

Two Florida prison guards and a former trainee have been charged in a plan to kill a former inmate who was about to be released. The Florida Attorney General's office announced the charges. The men were once responsible for guarding prisons, but now they are accused of a serious crime. An FBI informant, who had secretly joined a branch of the KKK called the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, had meetings with the three men. The informant said that Thomas Jordan Driver, 25, told him he had a fight with the former inmate and that he and David Elliot Moran wanted the man dead. "six feet under," according to court papers. Charles Thomas Newcomb, 22, was also involved.

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – A group of world powers, called the P5+1, reached a framework agreement with Iran on its nuclear program. on Thursday. The deal's success is still uncertain. The countries have until the end of June to finalize the details and write the full agreement. But the talks were still historic, especially for the U States and Iran, whose relationship has been stuck for years. The negotiations were not flashy, but they showed diplomacy at its best – and also at its busiest.

An improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle near the Somali city of Garowe on Monday morning. Six people died, including four aid workers from UNICEF. Somalia’s president said the attack was an attack on the country’s future.. The bombing happened around 8 a.m. in Garowe, the capital of the Puntland region. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. It happened just after another incident on Sunday, when three African Union soldiers were killed in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia.

Prince Harry arrived in Australia on Monday. He is 3 years old. He will spend four weeks there serving with the Australian military. He visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital, and paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier.. There was a crowd outside the memorial. Some people took photos of him, and one boy held a sign that said, "Red Heads Rule!" in honor of Harry's hair color. The Australian Defence Forces said last week that during his time in Australia, Harry will work and live with soldiers in several army regiments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth.

Australia, a key ally of the United States, has agreed to share some intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said the arrangement is informal and mainly focuses on monitoring Australians who travel to Iraq to fight with ISIS.. But one Australian politician called the move "dancing with the devil." Over the weekend, Bishop became the first Australian government minister in two years to visit Iran, and met with President Hassan Rouhani. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in a Monday interview Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while she was in Tehran.

Marseille, France (CNN) – Initial tests on the flight data recorder, also called the "black box," from the crashed Germanwings Flight 9525 show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally made the plane descend faster by using the controls. according to France's air accident investigation agency, the BEA. The black box was found on Thursday by recovery teams who had searched for days in the mountains of the French Alps where the plane crashed on March 24. The BEA said on Friday that its teams started studying the data right away.

CNN reported that a 110-day chase from Antarctic waters to the west African coast ended unexpectedly. when the crew of a suspected illegal fishing ship, the Thunder, were rescued by conservationists who had been chasing them. The environmental group Sea Shepherd had been tracking the Thunder since it was first spotted by their ship, the Bob Barker, in the Southern Ocean several months earlier. The Thunder had an Interpol " purple notice" because of suspected fraud and fishing crimes. The chase ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off west Africa, when the Bob Barker received a distress call from the Thunder.

Most days, 16-year-old Jason Zobott arrives at Huntley High School, in suburban Chicago around 7:30 a.m., just like many high school students. But what he does after that is different. Jason is in Huntley High’s blended learning program, which combines online learning with regular classroom classes. One-third of the school’s 2,700 students are part of this program. The school wants most students to join by 2015. "The online work helps me get my schoolwork done," said Zobott, a top student who also does many after-school activities. "I can learn on my own."

Garissa, Kenya (CNN) – After a deadly Al-Shabaab attack in Kenya, the Kenyan military carried out airstrikes against the group in Somalia. A military source said the strikes were not punishment for the recent attack at Garissa University College, that killed almost 50 people. The source said the military operations against Al-Sh-Shabaab bases in Somalia began in 2011 and and are still ongoing.. It is common for Kenyan military sources to stay anonymous when speaking to the media.

Pope Francis reminded the world that the Vatican is a country and that he serves as a moral leader during his usual Easter Mass speech. He said he is deeply troubled by the suffering caused by current wars and called for an end to violence everywhere. He especially asked for an end to bloodshed in Iraq and Syria and for help to reach people in need. He urged the global community not to ignore the huge humanitarian crisis in these countries or the struggles of the many refugees. He made this appeal in his "urbi et orbi" message, which means "to the city (Rome) and to the world."

CNN reported that Duke University students and faculty marched Wednesday afternoon, shouting "We are not afraid. We stand together," after a noose was found hanging from a tree on campus.. The noose was discovered near a student center at 2 a.m., the campus police asked anyone with information about the rope to contact them.. Photos of the noose spread quickly on social media, causing anger in the community. Later, hundreds of people gathered at a forum on the steps of Duke Chapel, close to where the noose was found. One speaker said, "You came here for the reason that you want to say with me, 'This is no Duke we will accept. This is no Duke we want. This is not the Duke we're here to experience.'"

A U.S. citizen, Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, 29, did not enter a plea during his first court appearance on Thursday. He was accused of helping terrorists by providing support, according to a court complaint. The charges are for planning to fight against U.S. forces overseas. He was deported from Pakistan to the U.S. CNN's counterterrorism analyst, Philip Mudd, said this news should be cause for celebration.

A Saudi border guard was killed in a fight with militants across the border in Yemen, the Saudi Press Agency reported. This is the first time Saudi Arabia has publicly confirmed a military death since it started bombing rebels in Yemen. The clash happened Wednesday night in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. The militants were in a mountainous area in Yemen. They fired on Saudi border troops, who returned fire. The dead guard was identified as Corporal Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki. Thirteen other Saudi soldiers were injured, but their injuries were not serious.

Dubai (CNN) I felt a little nervous about heading to the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. As the only Gulf national on the CNN team, I was expected to know about camel racing, a long-standing tradition here. But even though I tried to wear a kandora, the traditional UAE outfit, my modern way of life makes me feel completely out of place in this world. A friendly farm owner took us into the majlis — a special meeting area — where the camel owners were gathering. The room was big and beautifully decorated, like a fancy theater. The camel owners were sitting on the floor, eating a'aish, a traditional Arabic meal of fish and rice, which was served in front of them. The talk was loud and full of energy.

Havana, Cuba — Charlie Hill is sitting in a dark bar on a very sunny day in Havana. "Hey man," he says, his voice rough from smoking, nodding like he knows you’ve been looking for him. But a lot of people have been looking for Charlie Hill for a long time.. For 34 years, Cuba has kept him safe from being charged with killing a New Mexico police officer and hijing an airplane to Havana. Hill, now 65, finally agreed to talk to CNN after we spent two years trying to contact him. He says he’s now thinking about leaving Cuba and going back to the United States for the first time.

Misao Okawa, who was listed in Guinness World Records as the oldest person in the world,, has died at the age of 117. She died on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan, according to Tadahi Uchimura, a local official. She had three children, four grandchildren, and six great grandchildren. Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. Her family had a kimono shop in Osaka. Satoshi Yoshioka, an employee at the nursing home where she lived since 1997, said she was a kind, and quiet person who loved to eat. Her favorite foods were sushi and udon noodles. She had eaten a lot of cake on her birthday in March 2018.

Washington (CNN) – When the Missouri National Guard was sent to Ferguson, Missouri, to help deal with riots that broke out last year, they used strong military language like "enemy forces" and "adversaries" to describe the protesters. According to documents CNN obtained, the guard used these terms even though their main job was to support local police. Many community leaders and civil rights groups said the police had used too much force and made the situation worse during protests that happened on and off from August until the end of the year.

Mogadishu, Somalia (CNN) – Gunmen attacked the Somali education ministry in the capital on Tuesday after a suicide car bomb. The attack killed at least 12 people and injured 16 others, officials said. The Islamist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. The attack started when two suicide bombers exploded their cars at the entrance of the two-story building that houses the Ministry of Education, Culture and Higher Education. Somali National Security Ministry spokesman Mohamed Yusuf said. Five gunmen then entered the building and opened fire on people inside, he added.

Gregory Margolin is now 87 years old. He was just 16 when he joined the Soviet Red Army and fought against the Nazis in World War II. At the time, his family had to flee. He says he didn’t tell others he was Jewish, but it didn’t matter—so many people were dying all around him. This year, in Ukraine, he found himself in another war. He had once been a sniper and later became a commander in the army. His old military uniform still has the medals he earned during the war. time. His granddaughter, Liora, still listens in awe to his stories from the war. She can’t believe he lived through it.

More than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls are still missing. They were taken from their school dorms in Chibok, in northeastern Nigeria, over 365 days ago. The Nigerian government and the rest of the world did not stop this. It is wrong that this happened and even worse that so little has been done to find them. We should all feel ashamed. Shame that girls’ lives can be destroyed by violent extremists with no punishment. Shame that people quickly stop paying attention to such terrible events.

CNN. Video may have killed the radio star, but in Norway, it's digital that's replacing FM radio. In two years, Norway will be the first country in the world to completely stop using FM radio....... Instead, people will listen to the radio through digital signals. This doesn't mean no radio at all—just that people will need to switch to digital radio......... According to officials in Oslo, many people in Norway—a country with 5 million people—have already switched. Right now, only five radio stations are available on FM. But on the digital radio network, there are four times as many—20 stations. and half the country already listens this way, said Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey.

CNN says everyone loves a good comeback story — especially one as big as a dinosaur. For over 100 years, scientists thought the Brontosaurus was just a type of Apatosaurus. new research now says it should be its own separate dinosaur. In 1879, O.C. Marsh nameded the Brontosaurus after finding 25 crates of bones at Como Bluff, in Wyoming,, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. It was similar to, but not as big as, the Apatosaurus, which had been found a few years earlier. Marsh gave it the name "Brontosaurus," which means "thunder lizard."

Al Qaeda in Yemen, known as AQAP, has announced a reward of 20 kilograms of gold for anyone who kills or captures two Shia Muslim leaders. One is the Houthi rebel leader, Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi, and the other is former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh.  
  
  
  
  
  
  
The reward is worth about $774,000 in U.S. dollars.  
  
  
  
  
AQAP says it is is the "two heads of evil" and says it is offering the reward to anyone who kills or captures them.  
  
  
  
AQAP is one of many groups fighting for control of Yemen.

Before landing his gyrocopter on the Capitol lawn on Wednesday, Doug Hughes, a 61-year-old Florida postal worker, wrote about his plans and reasons on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. "The point of the flight is to show that there is corruption in Washington, DC, and to offer solutions to the deep-rooted problems in government," he said in a post titled "Your Pilot." He also said, "My flight is not a secret." He added that he had emailed info@barackobama.com before taking off, to tell the people in charge at the Capitol that he wasn't a threat. and that shooting him down would cause more trouble than just letting him deliver his letters to Congress.

The bad news for Rio de Janeiro keeps growing. After many dead fish were found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon, officials from Rio's legislative assembly announced on Monday they will investigate why the fish died.. This comes less than a year before Rio hosts the Olympics rowing and canoe events. The investigation will include other lakes and bays in the state where similar fish deaths have happened. They will work with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the State Secretariat for the Environment.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. But in a 58-year-old way, he's just starting to experience life. Simple things like using a fork, going out at night, or going to bed without someone watching over you — these are all new to him. Hinton spent almost 30 years on Alabama’s death row. Just one week ago, his murder convictions were overturned, and he left a county jail in Birmingham. "I have to pinch myself to believe I’m really free," he told CNN’s Brooke Baldwin. "It will take time, but I’ll get used to it." For 30 years, he mostly lived in a small 5-by-7-foot cell.

The opinion polls after the UK election debate showed no clear winner. The seven party leaders were David Cameron (Conservatives), Ed Miliband (Labour), Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrats), Nigel Farage (UKIP), Natalie Bennett (Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon (SNP), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru). Comres, which was commissioned by ITV to run the debate, found Cameron, Miliband, and Farage all tied for first with 21% each, while Sturgeon came in close behind with 20%. Another poll by ICM for The Guardian was slightly different: giving Miliband 25, Cameron 24, Farage 19, and Sturgeon 17.

CNN reports that Facebook might soon include "Just got served divorce papers" as a relationship status. — after a New York judge ruled that posting a divorce notice on Facebook is a valid way to serve divorce papers. in Brooklyn..... The woman, Ellanora Arthur Baidoo, has been trying to divorce her husband, Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku, for years, according to her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell. But they can't find him to serve the papers. Baidoo has called him several times, and he told her he has no fixed address and no job. —..... according to court documents.

It sounds like a scene from a sci-fi movie. Someone has a terrible accident and ends up in the hospital, brain dead and on life support. Doctors talk to the family about donating organs, but instead of saving up to eight lives, they’re asked to donate the whole body to save just one person—maybe someone who is paralyzed but has a sharp mind. The idea is to transplant a head onto a new body. Even though it sounds impossible, Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says we are getting close to making it real. He calls this project HEAVEN, which stands for Head Anastomosis Venture. Anastomosis means joining two parts together, like connecting them surgically.

Anthony Stokes was supposed to have a happy ending. But it ended Tuesday, police say, when he carjacked someone, broke into a house, shot at an older woman, led police on a high-speed chase, and died when his car hit a pole. In 2013, his family said an Atlanta hospital turned him down for a heart transplant. because he had a history of not following medical advice, according to a letter from the hospital. At the time, Mark Bell was speaking for the Stokes family.

The sun had not risen at Garissa University College.. Most students were still asleep in their beds. A few had gotten up to go to early morning Christian prayers. Then, the attack started. It began with an explosion and gunshots around 5 a.m on Thursday (10:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday) at the front gates of the school in Kenya. The attackers continued firing as they moved through the campus. The Red Cross said they stopped at a dorm for girls. At one point, they entered a room where Christians were gathered and took people hostage, said lecturer Joel Ayora.

A white casket was at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore while a gospel choir sang for a large crowd. people came to honor Freddie Gray. Gray, 25, died 15 days ago while in police custody after being arrested on a weapons charge. He died from a serious spinal cord injury. His death caused strong anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray’s death is part of a recent series of well-known cases where African Americans died during encounters with police. Many people are asking what really happened to Gray. His funeral brought in civil rights leaders, politicians, and family members of others who died in police custody.

I’ve been working in food since I was 14. but I didn’t start fighting for food rights until 2007. That was when a girl I knew—my wife had been mentoring—was caught digging in the trash looking for food. That moment changed me. I decided to create Food Policy Action and get involved in politics around food issues like hunger and factory farming. I didn’t do this alone. A big turning point was "The Meatrix," a 2003 video parody of "The Matrix" made by the GRACE Communications Foundation. It clearly showed how factory farming harms people’s health and the environment.

CNN's Dan Swangard knows what death looks like. As a doctor, he's seen patients die in hospitals, on morphine, feeling scared and anxious. He's also seen how long and hard dying can be, with family members watching helplessly. But now, his thoughts about death are personal. In 2013, he was diagnosed with a rare type of cancer that has spread. Doctors removed parts of his pancreas and liver, his entire spleen, and his gallbladder. The surgery was successful, but Swangard, who is 48, knows he has a high chance the cancer will come back.

CNN reported that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters attack Houthis and their allies in Aden. The Saudi source said the special forces were on the ground in noncombat roles, helping to coordinate and direct the fighting against Houthis and fighters loyal to former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. They also helped drop weapons and communication equipment by parachute. Meanwhile, Houthis withdrew from the presidential palace and other important areas in Aden after strong Saudi airstrikes. This withdrawal came after Houthis had taken control of the presidential palace the day before. The shift showed a change from their earlier gains.

A Detroit mother was arrested last month after police found the bodies of two of her children in a freezer.. She was formally charged this week with murder and torture. Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy said she was charged with killing her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry. The bodies were found on March 24 by a bailiff during a court-ordered eviction. Detroit Police Chief James Craig said the children's bodies were wrapped in plastic and were inside the freezer. The Wayne County medical examiner said Stoni died from multiple blunt force injuries and Stephen died from multiple blunt force injuries and burns.

Wladimir Klitschko, the world heavyweight boxing champion, is preparing for an important fight on April 25 against American boxer Bryant Jennings in New York. But his mind is still on the fight for democracy in Ukraine. Speaking from his training base in Miami, Klitschko said he is deeply upset by the ongoing war in his country. He said Ukraine is not the one starting the conflict, and that Russia is the one causing the problems. He added that Ukraine did not start any aggression against Russia.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" for the third time this weekend. He made a small nod to his roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman" during his opening monologue. Saying he's had a baby who is now 31, and a new girlfriend who is 28. — a reference to how much has changed since he first hosted in 1982. Fans hoping to see him fully play Batman or Beetlejuice were let down. — SNL cast members Taran Killam and Bobby Moynihan even sang a song asking him to play those characters. — but Keaton only gave a few jokes in return..

Just over a month ago, Kamron Taylor was convicted of murder in an Illinois court. He was then taken to an Illinois jail. Early Wednesday morning, while hiding outside his cell, Taylor attacked a correctional officer who was on duty. Taylor hit the officer, put on the officer’s uniform and took his keys. He then left the jail through the door and got into the officer’s brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox. The 23-year-old, who had been scheduled to be sentenced in May, is now missing.. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m. (9:30 a.m.)

A New York City detective has been suspended after being accused of stealing $300 during a raid on illegal cigarettes. Police spokesman Stephen Davis said the incident happened last Friday at the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn.. Surveillance video from a CNN affiliate, News 12 Brooklyn, shows Detective Ian Cyrus putting cash into a bag before leaving the store. The detectives had arrested two store employees for selling loose cigarettes. The store’s manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed the money was missing from a box. He first thought one of his employees took it. But when he checked the security footage, he was shocked by what he saw. He told News 12 Brooklyn he couldn’t believe it.

London (CNN) – A major robbery at Hatton Garden, which will likely be remembered as one of the biggest heists in London's history, took place over the holiday weekend. The thieves used powerful cutting tools and rapped down from above to get into the vault of a well-known 60-year-old safe deposit company in central London. They had as long as four days to search through the boxes, which were not fully counted. They are believed to have stolen hundreds of thousands of pounds in gems and cash. and possibly as much as £200 million (about $300 million), according to a former police official.

On April 2, South Africa will mark the anniversary of its first post-apartheid elections in 1994. This year, we is faced with another wave of violent attacks against African migrants. These attacks have sparked strong anger on social media, with people using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica to show unity and stand against the violence. Such repeated attacks on migrants and their property may suggest that South Africa's dream of a rainbow nation is not being fulfilled. That dream was not just about having people of different races living together, but also about everyone, no matter their race or class, being able to live with dignity.

In 1989, Ayatollah Khomeini said he was " drinking poison " when he agreed to a ceasefire that ended the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had played a key role in shaping Khomeini's regime, the Islamic Republic, which he had created just a year earlier, after Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini united both his supporters and opponents in fighting against Iraq. He kept the war going for eight years, even though Saddam had offered a ceasefire. This helped strengthen the Islamic Republic. By the time the war ended, the economy was broken, and many of his loyal volunteers were gone.

CNN says that the idea of sustainable development comes from the fact that uncontrolled capitalism is too strong and harmful to itself. The global economy is growing very fast—it doubles in size every generation. But Earth has limited resources, and a billion more people are born every 15 years. This rapid growth is now damaging the planet’s natural systems and the social systems that help people live good, decent lives. Sustainable development is a way to solve this worsening crisis. The truth is that raw capitalism is really just the economics of greed.

The United States has benefited greatly from being a space-faring nation..  
  
Space has helped strengthen national security, defense, and the economy.  
The U.S. military needs space-based systems like spy satellites, GPS, and communication satellites to deal with today’s conflicts, fight terrorism, and handle growing global threats.  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
But as the number of global threats is rising and the need for reliable access to space is growing, the U.S. faces a serious problem: it depends too much on Russian technology to carry out its national security duties.

On the one-year anniversary of when nearly 300 schoolgirls were kidnapped by Boko Haram in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai wrote an "open letter" to them. She said, "Like you, I was a target of militants who didn't want girls to go to school." Malala, who is 17, won the Nobel Peace Prize. She survived a Taliban attack in Pakistan because she had been speaking out about girls' right to education. In her letter, she asks the Nigerian government and the world to do more to find the missing girls.. Nigeria recently held an election.

Johannesburg (CNN) – South African troops were deployed Tuesday evening as part of a new government plan to stop violent attacks against immigrants. Their first stop was the Johannesburg suburb of Jeppestown, where the violence started on Friday. Police raided a hostel in Jeppestown on Tuesday while troops guarded the area. Earlier, Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said the government would send an unknown number of troops to places where police are too few to stop deadly attacks on immigrants. "This intervention is not an indictment on the police."

Eight Iranian border guards were killed in fights with armed militants near the border with Pakistan, according to Iranian state media. Three militants were killed by Iranian forces during the clashes on Monday in the town of Negur, southeastern Iran. The Iranian news agency IRNA said the militants had crossed into Iran from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistani authorities to find and arrest the remaining attackers.

CNN. If you love island-hopping, you should know that Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos has been named the world’s best island by TripAdvisor.. This year, it moved up one spot from number 2 last year, and pushed Ambergris Caye in Belize out of the top position. Ambergris Caye had been number 1 for two years running, but this year it fell completely out of the top 10..... The "Star Wars" universe is growing. At the Star Wars Celebration fan event in Anaheim, California, on Sunday, details about the 2016 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" were shared. Director Gareth Edwards, who also made "Godzilla," showed a short preview of the film. He also shared plot details for this "Star Wars" anthology movie, which Disney calls an "anthology" instead of a "spinoff." It stars Felicity Jones. The story takes place between "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode IV: A New Hope" (the first "Star Wars" movie, from 1977). A rebel group goes on a secret mission to steal the plans for the Death Star.. Jones will play a rebel soldier

Tehran, Iran (CNN) – A Persian proverb says, "A good year starts with a good spring." For many Iranians, the recent decision by Tehran and six world powers — the U States, UK, France, Germany, Russia, and China — to continue nuclear talks under a "joint comprehensive plan of action" is a sign that this year’s Norouz, the Persian New Year that began on March 21, will be a good one. Even though some tough, conservative voices may complain that the first agreement isn’t exactly what they wanted, many people see it as real progress — and that’s what they care about.

One Israeli man was killed and another was injured in an incident near Hebrew University in Jerusalem on Wednesday night. police believe it was a terror attack. A 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem drove into two people waiting at a bus stop in the French Hill area. The victim who died was identified as Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26. A 20-year-old woman is still in serious condition. The driver has been arrested and is being investigated by Israel’s General Security Services.

An art collection owned by the late Hollywood star Lauren Bacall has been put up for sale. The collection, which includes pieces by major 20th-century artists, was on display in New York on March 31, after being shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles. Bacall, who died in August 2014 at age 89, first became famous in 1944 with her film "To Have and Have Not." That was also when she met her future husband, Humphrey Bogart. At the 2015 Golden Globes, George Clooney remembered Bacall in his award-winning speech.

Kiev, Ukraine (CNN) – People in Kiev are asking who is killing the supporters of Ukraine’s former President Viktor Yanukovych. The idea isn’t completely new, but it came back into focus this week after two high-profile killings in the capital. One was a former lawmaker linked to Yanukovych, and the other was a Ukrainian journalist known for supporting Russia. Oleg Kalashnikov, the former lawmaker, was shot dead just after 7 p.m. on Wednesday at the entrance of his apartment building.

Same-sex civil unions will soon be recognized in Chile. The country has joined several other South American nations by passing a new law.. President Michelle Bachelet signed the law on Monday. She said this is an important step toward treating gay and straight couples the same. The law will start in six months. It will give legal rights to couples living together, whether they are two men, two women, or a man and a woman. The government says about 2 million people will benefit from this new law.

When you fly to visit Grandma in Florida, look down. When you take the kids to see the talking mouse or go to South Beach for sun and fun, sit by the window and think about what you see below. Because few places show how people made a big mistake—and how hard it is to fix it—like the Everglades. As you fly into Miami or Orlando, it may look like a wet, ugly land full of dangerous animals: snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. One scientist caught over 365,000 mosquitoes in a single trap in one night..

CNN reported that ISIS fighters took over Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. The camp had been under siege and bombing by Syrian forces for over two years. and its people were already suffering. In early April, residents woke up to find ISIS militants in control after defeating local militia groups. One resident, who did not want to be named, told CNN that ISIS fighters killed people in the streets. "They killed three people right in front of others," he said. Now, ISIS controls almost all of Yarmouk.

China's internet censors have long used the "Great Firewall" to block Chinese people from reading critical articles from Western news sites or watching other content they don’t approve of. But now, according to a study released on Friday, they’ve created a new tool. They’ve used it to attack servers outside China, including in the United States. The researchers who studied it have called this new tool the "Great Cannon." It works openly, right in plain view. The study says that attacking servers so openly and easily inside another country—especially the U States— will likely upset other nations. But the researchers think Beijing may have expected that.

The investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found any evidence about Lubitz's motive. But a spokesman for the prosecutor's office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said on Monday that Lubitz had suicidal thoughts at some point before he started his aviation career. The spokesman, Christoph Kumpa, said investigators found no notes, messages, or conversations where Lubitz explained his reasons or admitted to any plans. But medical records show Lubitz was suicidal in the past and had therapy. This happened before he got his pilot's license, Kumpa said.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his fighters would not leave major cities or government buildings. He told a TV audience, "Anyone who thinks we will give up is just dreaming." The statement came after over three weeks of airstrikes by a Saudi-led coalition. The goal was to weaken the Houthi group, which had taken control of the capital, Sanaa, in January and forced President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi to flee.
